narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that, in combination, signal a higher risk of departure compared to colleagues who are expected to stay.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. Unlike most employees predicted to stay—where only about 23% report such offers—your access to alternatives pushes the prediction strongly toward leaving, as it suggests you have viable options elsewhere.

Next, your 11+ years of total professional experience stands out. While the majority of employees expected to remain have 5 years or fewer of overall experience, your extensive background appears to increase the model's assessment of your mobility and likelihood of moving on.

Finally, your difficult work-life balance also contributes to the prediction of leaving. This is relatively uncommon among those expected to stay, where most report a medium or easy balance, making this factor another notable push away from long-term retention.

The organization should consider discussing ways to improve your work-life balance and exploring how to make your current role more competitive against external offers. For your part, reflecting on whether these opportunities better align with your long-term goals could help clarify your next steps. (218 words)
